entities.summary:
Guillaume de Harsigny was a French doctor and court physician to Charles V of France, a position he held from 1371 to 1393. Born in France, de Harsigny studied medicine at the University of Paris and later became a prominent physician in his own right, known for his expertise in pharmacology and his work on the treatment of plague.

As a key figure in the royal court, de Harsigny played a significant role in the development of medical knowledge and practice during the late Middle Ages. He was one of the first physicians to recognize the importance of quarantine in preventing the spread of disease, a concept that would later become a cornerstone of public health policy.

De Harsigny's legacy extends beyond his own time and place, influencing the development of medicine and public health in Europe and beyond. His work on pharmacology and plague treatment continues to be studied by scholars today, and his commitment to the importance of quarantine remains a model for modern public health policy.

"The art of medicine is long, but life is short," de Harsigny once said, a quote that reflects his understanding of the importance of timely and effective medical care.
